questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, you must wait for the air compressor to build a minimum of ____ in both the primary and secondary systems.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, wait for the air compressor to build at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: The ____ tells a driver how much pressure is in the air tanks.
questions.explanation: The supply pressure gauge shows the driver how much air pressure is in the vehicle's air tanks.

questions.question: If you are being tailgated, you should:
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, create more space in front of your vehicle so they can pass safely. Do not drive faster, as this only increases danger.

questions.question: What is a tire load?

options.text: The minimum safe weight a tire can carry
The maximum safe weight a tire can carry
The weight of the air within a fully inflated tire

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe weight a tire can carry
questions.explanation: Tire load is the maximum weight a tire can safely carry at a specified pressure. This information is printed on the side of the tire.

questions.question: While driving downhill, you should brake until you reach a speed that is ____ below your safe speed, then release the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: While driving downhill, brake until your speed is 5 mph below your safe speed. Then release the brake pedal. Repeat this process as needed.

questions.question: Roads are most slippery right after it begins to rain because:

options.text: The water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
The gravel gets washed to the middle of the lane.
Some tires are not designed for rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: The water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, water mixes with oil on the road surface, creating a slippery and dangerous mixture.

questions.question: If your truck or trailer catches fire, you should:

options.text: Park in a congested area near trees.

questions.explanation: If your vehicle catches fire, move it away from the road and park in an open area away from plants and other vehicles. Do not go to a service station.

questions.question: A driver should always:

options.text: Drive faster than the posted speed limit.

questions.explanation: Always watch the road ahead for potential hazards. Plan how you would handle dangerous situations if they occur.

questions.question: If a roadway is covered by fog, it is best for you to:
questions.explanation: Driving in fog is dangerous. Avoid driving when fog is present if possible.

questions.question: Regarding winter driving, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: Front tires should have a tread depth of at least 4/32 an inch.
Rear tires should have a tread depth of at least 2/32 an inch.
Use a gauge to verify that each tire has a safe tread depth.

questions.explanation: In winter, your tires need good tread. Front tires need at least 4/32 inch of tread. Rear tires need at least 2/32 inch of tread. Use a gauge to check tread depth. Do not deflate your tires.

questions.question: If you find something unsafe during a pre-trip inspection, what should you do?

options.text: Continue driving and schedule a mechanic appointment after your trip ends.
Let a more experienced driver use the truck.
Avoid using the unsafe parts, but continue driving normally.

questions.explanation: You must repair any safety issue found during a pre-trip inspection before driving. It is illegal to drive an unsafe vehicle.

questions.question: When using controlled braking in an emergency, what should you do?

options.text: Press the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
Press the brakes with about half your normal force.
Press the brakes until the wheels lock.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
questions.explanation: For controlled braking, press the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels. Keep your steering movements small while braking this way.

questions.question: What happens when driving in extremely hot weather?

options.text: You should not drive at all.
You must remove oil from the engine.
It is safer to use less coolant.
Tire pressure can increase to dangerous levels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tire pressure can increase to dangerous levels.
questions.explanation: Hot weather causes air in your tires to expand, increasing tire pressure. To prevent engine overheating, make sure you have enough oil and coolant.

questions.question: What should you do if an aggressive driver confronts you?
questions.explanation: Get out of the aggressive driver's way. Do not make eye contact or gesture at them. Report them to authorities when you can do so safely.

questions.question: If spring brakes are activated, you should never:

options.text: Release air from the air storage tanks.

questions.explanation: Never apply the brake pedal when spring brakes are activated. Using both springs and air pressure together can damage the brakes.

questions.question: After the engine starts, all warning lights and buzzers should:

options.text: Turn off once you start moving.

questions.explanation: Warning lights and buzzers should turn off right away after the engine starts. This includes the charging circuit light, oil light, coolant light, and ABS light.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, you will be checked on traffic awareness. Which should you NOT do?
questions.explanation: Check traffic and use your mirrors regularly during the driving skills test. Always check your mirrors when approaching intersections. Watch for pedestrians in all areas where they might be present.

questions.question: When entering a curve, you should:
questions.explanation: Slow down and shift to a lower gear before entering a curve.

questions.question: The drive shaft should be:
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, check that the drive shaft is straight and not bent or cracked.

questions.question: When operating a CMV, what is required regarding safety belts?

options.text: You do not need to wear one.
You only need to wear one if your vehicle has no airbags.
You only need to wear one if you are hauling more than 1,000 pounds.

questions.explanation: A safety belt is your best protection in a crash. You must always wear a safety belt while operating a CMV.

questions.question: For parallel parking on the right side, you should:

options.text: Back past the space, then pull forward into it.
Drive forward past the space, then back into it.
Drive forward directly into the space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive forward past the space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: Drive past the parking space first. Then back into it, keeping the rear of your vehicle close to the rear of the space. Your vehicle must be completely inside the space boundaries.

questions.question: Texting while driving:

options.text: Is allowed if your employer asks a question.

questions.explanation: Texting and reading text messages while driving is illegal.

questions.question: After you start the engine, oil pressure should reach normal level:
questions.explanation: Watch the gauges after starting the engine. Oil pressure should rise to normal within a few seconds.

questions.question: Which crime would NOT disqualify someone from a hazardous materials endorsement?
questions.explanation: Certain crimes disqualify a person from getting a hazardous materials endorsement for seven years. These include arson, robbery, and dishonesty. Serious crimes like murder cause lifetime disqualification. Littering does not disqualify someone.

questions.question: A distracted driver may be:

options.text: Focused on using their cell phone.
Not talking to anyone in the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Focused on using their cell phone.
questions.explanation: A distracted driver may drift between lanes, drive at inconsistent speeds, use a cell phone, or talk to passengers. These signs show the driver is not focused on the road.

questions.question: When you start a vehicle, the coolant temperature gauge should:

options.text: Slowly rise to normal operating temperature.
Jump quickly to normal operating temperature.
Flash until reaching normal operating temperature.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly rise to normal operating temperature.
questions.explanation: Watch the gauges after starting the engine. The coolant temperature gauge should gradually rise to normal operating temperature.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a driving distraction?
questions.explanation: Anything that takes attention from driving is a distraction. This includes eating, drinking, smoking, and adjusting audio or climate controls. Checking mirrors is a necessary part of safe driving.

questions.question: Before going down a hill, you should:
questions.explanation: Before going down a hill, shift to a low gear. Gravity will make your vehicle go faster going downhill.

questions.question: When entering a foggy area, you should:

options.text: Stop on the side of the road.

questions.explanation: Slow down when entering fog. Use low beam headlights. Do not pass others or stop on the side of the road. If possible, avoid driving in fog entirely.

questions.question: Federal and state laws require:

options.text: Drivers to inspect their vehicles regularly.
Drivers to inspect their vehicles only if they think something is wrong.
Drivers to inspect their vehicles only when traveling out-of-state.
Drivers to inspect their vehicles only if carrying hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers to inspect their vehicles regularly.
questions.explanation: Commercial drivers must inspect their vehicles before every trip. Regular inspections help find problems before they become dangerous and expensive.

questions.question: Most heavy-duty vehicles use ____ air brake systems.
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles have dual air brake systems.

questions.question: How can you tell if a vehicle has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS)?

options.text: A sticker on the control panel.
A yellow light on the dashboard.
The letters "ABS" on the brake pedal.
A metal plate on the inside of the driver's door.

questions.correctAnswerText: A yellow light on the dashboard.
questions.explanation: A yellow ABS warning light on the dashboard means your vehicle has an Anti-Lock Braking System.

questions.question: How many driver's licenses can a person have?

options.text: Two — one for cars and one for trucks.
One for each state where you plan to drive.
A regular license from one state and a CDL from another.

questions.explanation: You can have only one driver's license. States share driver information in a computer database to prevent duplicate licenses.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, where should you place the weight?

options.text: Only on the left side, if possible.
Only on the right side, if possible.

questions.explanation: Place cargo weight as low as possible. If weight is too high, the trailer may tip over.

questions.question: How often must you check that cargo is secured?
questions.explanation: Check cargo is secure before starting, within the first 50 miles, and then every 150 miles or three hours.

questions.question: Why is it important to inspect your vehicle before a trip?

options.text: To fill time before the trip.

questions.explanation: The most important reason to inspect your vehicle is to keep you and others safe on the road. Vehicle inspections before each trip are required by state and federal law.

questions.question: What does the air compressor governor do?

options.text: Controls when air is pumped into the air storage tanks.
Controls how fast air leaves the air storage tanks.
Controls the temperature of air entering the air storage tanks.
Controls the temperature of air leaving the air storage tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Controls when air is pumped into the air storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor decides when the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.

questions.question: What should a driver do if they feel tired while driving?
questions.explanation: If you feel drowsy, safely pull over and sleep. Caffeine and other stimulants are dangerous because fatigue can return suddenly when they wear off.

questions.question: What happens if air pressure in the tanks drops below 60 psi?

options.text: The vehicle will not shift out of gear.

questions.explanation: When air pressure falls below 60 psi, a low pressure warning signal activates. This may be a warning light or a wig wag.

questions.question: What should you check about tire wear during a vehicle inspection?

options.text: Inside tires are more worn than outside tires.
Outside tires are more worn than inside tires.
Middle of tires are more worn than the outside.

questions.explanation: Check that your tire treads are worn evenly across the tire.

questions.question: What happens if a truck's Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) stops working?

options.text: The truck will have no brakes at all.
The truck should only be driven slowly.
The truck will still have brakes.
The truck will lose brakes on its left side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck will still have brakes.
questions.explanation: If the ABS system fails, the truck will still have regular brakes. You can drive and brake normally.

questions.question: What can happen if the exhaust system is broken?

options.text: Poisonous fumes may get into the cab.
Poisonous fumes may come out the back of the muffler.
It may cause problems with a full trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Poisonous fumes may get into the cab.
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system can let poisonous fumes into the cab or sleeper berth. Check your exhaust system regularly for damage.

questions.question: How does a vehicle's center of gravity affect driving?

options.text: It usually does not affect how the vehicle handles.
It is very important to how safely you can drive the vehicle.
You should not worry about it when loading cargo.
It only matters if your route has many hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is very important to how safely you can drive the vehicle.
questions.explanation: A vehicle's center of gravity is very important for safe driving. Always load cargo as low as possible to keep the center of gravity low.

questions.question: How do you use the stab braking method in an emergency?

options.text: Press the brakes fully until the wheels lock. Release them until the wheels roll again. Repeat this process.
Press the brakes halfway while keeping the wheels rolling.
Press the brakes fully, let the wheels lock, and hold the brakes until the vehicle stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brakes fully until the wheels lock. Release them until the wheels roll again. Repeat this process.
questions.explanation: Stab braking means pressing the brakes fully until they lock. Then release them until the wheels start rolling. Repeat this pattern to stop.

questions.question: How should you change lanes?

options.text: Make the move with a jerking motion.
You do not need to use a turn signal.

questions.explanation: Change lanes slowly and smoothly to stay in control. This also gives other drivers time to move if you did not see them. Always use a turn signal.

questions.question: Which sign shows that you are drowsy while driving?

options.text: Your eyes blur or go out of focus on their own.
You have trouble keeping your head up.
You drift from lane to lane.

questions.explanation: Signs of drowsy driving include eyes that blur or close on their own, trouble holding your head up, and drifting between lanes.

questions.question: What happens if the engine has no oil?

options.text: The vehicle will use less gas.
The engine can be destroyed very quickly.
The ABS will not work right.
The windshield wipers will not work.

questions.correctAnswerText: The engine can be destroyed very quickly.
questions.explanation: Engine oil is critical. The engine will be severely damaged very quickly if it runs without oil.

questions.question: What should you do in an emergency while driving?

options.text: Stopping is not always the best choice.
Always turn on your flashers to warn others.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping is not always the best choice.
questions.explanation: Stopping is not always the safest action in an emergency. It is usually safer to steer away from danger to avoid a crash.

questions.question: How do you do an offset back/right parking maneuver?

options.text: Pull straight forward, then back to the right.
Pull straight forward, then back to the left.
Pull forward to the right, then back in a straight line.
Pull forward to the left, then back in a straight line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull straight forward, then back to the right.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/right maneuver, pull straight forward first. Then back up to the right. Your vehicle must stay within the parking space lines.

questions.question: You should always be able to stop within what distance?

options.text: The distance you can see ahead.
One minute after you hit the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The distance you can see ahead.
questions.explanation: You must be able to stop within the distance you can see. Slow down when visibility is poor.
